title: Turn stationary exponential tails into uniform nominal transient moments
statement: For ANY invariant Markov kernel, P_t(x,A)<=pi(A)/pi(x), because the stationary sum contains that nonnegative initial-state term. With the conditional-Poisson bounds this yields P_x0(|N_t|>s)<=min(1,exp(D0+A0-s)) uniformly for ALLt>=0. Integrating the shifted tail gives E_x0(1+|N_t|)^m<=C_m(1+D0+A0)^m for every fixedm,C_m=1+3m!, with analogous stationary moments. The initial inverse-atom factor shifts an exponential tail threshold; it is not used as an exponentially poor multiplicative moment bound. The lemma applies also to the fixed-R global nominal clock. For an initial law with sufficiently high polynomial moments, integrate the polynomial-in-|x| bound; hence D123 nominal evolutions from perturbed stationarity are paid once sufficiently HIGH perturbed stationary moments really hold. It does NOT establish perturbed recurrence/moments or control a process that no longer preservespi.
